readerQuestion: How can I monitor internet interruptions in Home Assistant without mistaking one failed ping, a DNS problem, or a missing sensor for a whole-home outage?
directAnswer: Keep separate router, Cloudflare and Google Ping readings; warn locally only when both external readings have each been off for two minutes. Compare the router, DNS and real-service behavior before assigning a cause. Start with the two-Toggle-helper rehearsal, not a router interruption. The example measures selected IPv4 ping paths and does not certify internet, ISP or application health.
originalContribution: Sections #history, #warning and #rehearsal combine a five-row interpretation table, a hypothetical 19:10/19:12 failure sequence, a complete two-source warning with held conditions and periodic rechecks, and a harmless two-helper exercise with expected pass/fail outcomes. The recipe separates observed failure from missing data and distinguishes a retained warning from live status.
limitations: Documentation research, static YAML validation and website browser checks only. No live Home Assistant execution, household network testing, measured detection latency, ISP outage measurement or phone-delivery test is claimed. Ping targets can fail or be filtered independently. IPv4 reachability does not establish IPv6, DNS, HTTPS, device discovery, device commands or device-initiated updates. Short interruptions and Home Assistant downtime are not fully recorded. UI labels may differ by installed release. Source-link HTTP checks returned 200 for all 13 distinct published primary URLs.
proofreadFixes: Final pass replaced the unexplained ISP acronym in the TLDR and defined resolver beside the DNS recommendation. Reworded the table's routing/filtering language into concrete next checks. Expanded the ping limitation to distinguish discovery, commands and device-initiated updates. Clarified that dismissing an ongoing warning permits it to return on the periodic recheck, and bounded the retained-notification explanation to continued Home Assistant operation. Added primary links for state-duration conditions, the five-minute trigger and Run actions bypassing conditions; made both code blocks keyboard focusable. Verified the example requires both exact off states for two minutes, keeps unknown/unavailable out of the outage conditions, and uses only a local notification action. No automated proofreading is described as human or expert review.

claimChecks.claim: Ping creates a connectivity binary sensor, uses a 30-second default interval and probes from Home Assistant to the configured host. Default polling is retained; no YAML polling override or router-security change is prescribed.
Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 address is a public IPv4 resolver address. Using it as a ping target does not reconfigure the household DNS resolver, and the example is explicitly limited to IPv4 probes.
Ping does not measure DNS resolution; ICMP can be deprioritized. Successful or failed ping is not proof of all application paths or of a specific ISP fault.
Connectivity labels map to stored on/off states; unknown and unavailable are separate states. The warning checks off exactly and leaves missing readings visible on the dashboard.
The state trigger can watch multiple entities with to: off and a duration. Its pending for wait resets on a restart or automation reload, so no exact downtime continuity is promised.

Each state condition independently requires its source to have been off for two minutes. This prevents a failure in just one probe, a brief second failure or an unavailable source from satisfying the illustrated warning rule.
minutes: /5 schedules periodic evaluations. These revisit an ongoing condition after a missed transition; they do not reconstruct past observations while Home Assistant was off.

persistent_notification.create shows a frontend notice; a reused notification_id overwrites it. The automation does not dismiss it on recovery and may recreate it after dismissal while failure continues.
Local Push requires a working direct connection and platform-specific configuration. It does not provide an independent outbound connection to an off-site phone during a total home internet outage.

DNS IP defaults to an OpenDNS external-IP lookup; explicit hostname/resolver settings examine a chosen DNS path. Its two-minute polling and retry/unavailable behavior are kept separate from ping warnings.

The supplied History graph uses core type, title, hours_to_show and entity entries; it requires no custom card. Website verification confirms the YAML displays intact, but the guide does not claim the Home Assistant card itself was run.
Toggle helpers hold on/off states independently of hardware. The rehearsal changes only dedicated helpers and produces a dedicated test notification.
Run actions skips triggers and conditions, so the reader must change practice helper states and inspect traces to verify the complete condition path.

incomingLinkOpportunities.section: What an availability alert can miss
incomingLinkOpportunities.readerReason: A reader seeing several cloud devices fail together can next inspect the household internet path without interpreting each unavailable entity as an independent device fault.
A reader who understands which functions need internet can next create a local record of suspected interruptions and learn why an off-site phone alert needs a working delivery path.
